# AF 第四章 原文（重制基线）

## Chapter 4

[P01] By late summer, news of Animal Farm had spread across half the county（县）. Every day Snowball and Napoleon sent out pigeons to tell nearby animals about the uprising（起义） and teach them the tune of 'Animals of England'. Mr. Jones sat in the Red Lion at Willingdon. He complained that a pack of good-for-nothing animals had turned him out. The other farmers felt sorry for him, but at first gave little help.

[P02] Deep down, each of them wondered if he could turn Jones's bad luck into his own good. Luckily, the owners of the two farms next to Animal Farm did not get along. One was Foxwood（狐林）, a big, old, neglected（被忽视） farm. Its owner, Mr. Pilkington, was a relaxed gentleman farmer who spent most of his time fishing or hunting. The other farm, Pinchfield（窄地）, was smaller and better kept. Its owner, Mr. Frederick, was a tough（艰难）, clever man who was always in lawsuits（诉讼） and known for making hard bargains（交易）.

[P03] These two disliked（讨厌） each other and could not agree on anything. But they were both afraid of the uprising on Animal Farm. They did not want their own animals to learn about it. At first they laughed at the idea of animals running a farm. It would end in two weeks, they said. They spread the news that the animals there were always fighting and were quickly starving（挨饿） to death.

[P04] Later, the animals did not die of hunger. So Frederick and Pilkington changed their words. They said terrible things happened on Animal Farm. They said the animals ate each other, hurt each other with hot horseshoes（马蹄铁）, and shared their females. They said this came from fighting against Nature's laws. But people did not really believe these stories. Stories of a wonderful farm, where humans were driven out and animals ran things themselves, kept going around. All that year, a wave of rebellion（造反） ran through the countryside.

[P05] Gentle bulls（公牛） turned wild. Sheep broke hedges（树篱） and ate clover. Cows kicked over pails（桶）. Hunters（猎人） fell over fences. Everyone knew the tune and words of 'Animals of England'. It spread fast. People were angry but pretended it was funny. They said animals could not sing such silly rubbish. Any animal caught singing was beaten at once. Yet the song could not be stopped.

[P06] Blackbirds（黑鸟） sang it in the hedges. Pigeons cooed（咕咕叫） it in the elm（榆树） trees. It mixed with the smithies（铁匠铺）' noise and the church bells. People were secretly afraid. They felt it told of their bad end. In early October, the corn was cut and piled, and some was threshed（打谷）. Then many pigeons flew down to Animal Farm's yard, very excited.

[P07] Jones and his men, with six others from Foxwood and Pinchfield, came in through the gate and up the path（小路） to the farm. They all had sticks, but Jones walked in front with a gun. They wanted to take back the farm. The animals knew this would happen and were ready. Snowball had read an old book about Julius（朱利叶斯） Caesar（凯撒）'s wars. He led the defence（防御）. He gave orders fast, and in two minutes every animal was in place. When the men came near, Snowball began the first attack.

[P08] All thirty-five pigeons flew over the men's heads and dropped on them. While the men were busy, the geese rushed out and pecked（啄） their legs. The men drove the geese off with sticks. Then Snowball began his second attack. Muriel, Benjamin, and all the sheep, with Snowball leading, pushed and butted the men from every side, while Benjamin hit them with his small hoofs.

[P09] But the men were too strong for them, with sticks and heavy boots. Snowball squealed（尖叫）—the signal（信号） to run back. All the animals turned and ran through the gate into the yard. The men shouted in triumph（胜利） and rushed after them in disorder（混乱）. This was just what Snowball wanted. As soon as the men were inside the yard, the three horses, the three cows, and the other pigs came out behind them and cut them off.

[P10] Snowball gave the signal to attack. He ran straight at Jones. Jones raised his gun and fired. The shots cut Snowball's back, and a sheep fell dead. Snowball did not stop. He threw his fifteen stone（石头） at Jones's legs. Jones fell into a pile of dung（粪便） and his gun flew from his hands. But the most frightening thing was Boxer. He stood up on his back legs and hit out with his big iron hoofs（蹄）. His first blow killed a stable-lad（马童） from Foxwood.

[P11] When the men saw this, some dropped their sticks and ran away. They were afraid, and all the animals chased（追赶） them around the yard. The animals pushed, kicked, bit, and stepped on them. Even the cat jumped onto a man's shoulders and put her claws（爪子） into his neck. When the way was clear, the men ran out of the yard to the main road.

[P12] And so, five minutes after they came in, they ran away in shame, going back the same way they had come. A flock（羊群） of geese hissed after them and pecked at their legs all the way. All the men were gone except one. Back in the yard, Boxer was pushing with his hoof（蹄） at the stable-lad (马童), who lay face down in the mud, trying to turn him over.

[P13] The boy did not move. "He is dead," said Boxer sadly. "I forgot my iron shoes. Who will believe I did not do it on purpose?" "No pity, comrade（同志）!" cried Snowball. Blood was still dripping from Snowball's wounds."War is war. The only good human being is a dead one." "I do not want to kill anyone," Boxer said, with tears in his eyes. "Where is Mollie?" someone cried. Mollie was missing. Everyone was afraid the men had hurt her or taken her away.

[P14] In the end, they found her hiding in her stall（畜栏）. Her head was under the hay（干草） in the manger（食槽）. She ran away when the gun went off. The others came back and found the stable-lad（马童） was only stunned（震惊）. He was better and had run off. The animals came together again, very excited. Each told his own story of the fight loudly. They had a party for the win. They put up the flag and sang 'animals of England' many times. Then they buried the sheep who was killed, and planted a hawthorn（山楂） bush on her grave（坟墓）.

[P15] At the grave, Snowball made a short speech. He said all animals must be ready to die for Animal Farm. The animals agreed to make a military（军事） decoration（装饰）: "Animal Hero, First Class." They gave it to Snowball and Boxer. It was a brass（黄铜） medal—some old horse-brasses（铜牌） found in the harness（马具）-room. It was to be worn on Sundays and holidays. They also made "Animal Hero, Second Class" for the dead sheep. They talked about what to call the battle.

[P16] In the end, they called it the Battle of the Cowshed（牛棚）, because the ambush（埋伏） started there. They found Jones's gun in the mud. They decided to put it at the foot of the Flagstaff, like a piece of artillery, and fire it twice a year: on October 12, the anniversary（周年） of the Battle of the Cowshed, and on Midsummer Day, the anniversary of the uprising.
